pages: Dusk on a black shale cliff path above a jade-green bay: seven-year-old Sella, dark hair in two braids, wearing a bright yellow oilskin rain-slicker with its hood down, walks uphill beside her grandmother, an old woman in a grey wool shawl. Each carries a small brass lantern on a hook. A row of slim iron lamp posts runs away up the ridge, each already holding a small warm flame, and below them a steep slate-roofed fishing town and little boats on the water. The eye lands on the two of them walking together with their lanterns. no written words, letters, numbers, captions, logos, borders, or watermark

The far end of the headland: a single small brass lantern alone on a slim iron post at the very edge of a black rocky point, furthest from the town, where the wind has room to be itself. It is clearly the smallest lamp of the coast. Grass bends in the wind, the sea lies far below, and the warm lit line of the nearer ridge is small and far away behind. The eye rests on the one lonely little lamp. no written words, letters, numbers, captions, logos, borders, or watermark

Close on Sella, the seven-year-old girl with dark hair in two braids in a bright yellow oilskin rain-slicker, tapping the glass of a small brass lantern twice with her knuckle and bending to blow gently at its wick. A tiny grey puff of smoke comes out and the wick stays dark. Her grandmother in the grey shawl watches from just behind, holding her own lantern. The eye lands on the girl's knuckle against the glass and the small dead puff of smoke. no written words, letters, numbers, captions, logos, borders, or watermark

Sella's grandmother, an old woman in a grey wool shawl with a weathered kind face, holds out a small stoppered glass jar of pale golden eiderdown oil to seven-year-old Sella in the bright yellow oilskin rain-slicker, who reaches up and takes the jar in both hands. The little glass jar of glowing amber oil is the centre of the picture, held between an old hand and a child's small hands. The unlit brass lantern stands on the stone beside them with a thread of grey smoke still rising from it. The eye lands on the small glowing jar of oil passing from the old woman's hands into the little girl's hands. no written words, letters, numbers, captions, logos, borders, or watermark

Seven-year-old Sella with dark braids and a bright yellow oilskin rain-slicker tips one careful thin finger of pale golden oil from a small glass jar onto the wick of a brass lantern and touches a lit taper to it. The flame catches at once and leaps up tall and gold, and far below the whole bay has turned soft luminous jade-green. The eye lands on the tall golden flame she has just made. no written words, letters, numbers, captions, logos, borders, or watermark

Seven-year-old Sella with dark braids in a bright yellow oilskin rain-slicker has stepped back and stands looking away down the ridge, her small face disappointed. The brass lanterns nearest her in the foreground burn bright and gold, while far out on the black point a ninth lantern is only a faint dim smudge, clearly weaker than all the others. The eye travels from the bright near flames to the tiny dying one in the distance. no written words, letters, numbers, captions, logos, borders, or watermark

Seven-year-old Sella with dark braids in a bright yellow oilskin rain-slicker runs quickly back down a flight of wet black stone steps, holding the front of her coat up out of the puddles and glancing back over her shoulder. In her other hand she has a small tin roll of pale trimmed lamp wicks. The sea is below the steps and the ridge of lit lanterns is above. The eye lands on the running child and the little roll of wicks in her hand. no written words, letters, numbers, captions, logos, borders, or watermark

One child only: seven-year-old Sella, dark hair in two braids, in a bright yellow oilskin rain-slicker, crouches alone at the far black point with her face close to an open brass lantern. With her teeth she holds the limp end of a thin grey burnt-out old wick, and with both hands she presses a thick fat fresh cream-coloured lamp wick down into the lantern. No other person is present. Above her the lantern's flame lifts up bright and tall into the sea wind. The eye lands on the fat fresh pale wick in the child's hands against the bright flame. no written words, letters, numbers, captions, logos, borders, or watermark

Seven-year-old Sella with dark braids in a bright yellow oilskin rain-slicker walks back up the black shale ridge path, counting on the fingers of one hand as she goes. Behind her all nine iron posts stand lit in a long line of small warm flames along the cliff. Below, one by one, little fishing boats row safely into the jade-green bay and the town's windows are warm. The eye lands on the girl counting with the nine lights marching away behind her. no written words, letters, numbers, captions, logos, borders, or watermark

At the top of the wet black stone steps, seven-year-old Sella with dark braids in a bright yellow oilskin rain-slicker stands close beside her grandmother in the grey wool shawl, and the old woman's arm is around the girl's shoulders as both smile. All around them the nine small brass lanterns stand burning in a wide ring on their iron posts, like a ring of little suns, against the dark blue evening and the sea. The eye lands on the two of them smiling inside the ring of nine small golden lights. no written words, letters, numbers, captions, logos, borders, or watermark
